alarms.title: Part too hot for the next layer
alarms.operator_title: Part too hot for the next layer
alarms.operator_message: The part is still too hot. The robot is waiting before layer 4.
alarms.technical_detail: Interpass temperature 310 °C after 4 minutes of waiting; the limit is 200 °C. The small repair area on a thin wall holds heat. Starting now would widen and lower the bead and coarsen the grain structure.

ground_truth.root_cause: Heat accumulation in a thin section (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Wider, lower beads; worse microstructure; distortion.

expected_response.resolved_when: Temperature drops below 200 °C and the next layer starts.

hints: Waiting is normal here. Hot metal makes the next layer run and sag.
Watch the temperature curve; it should go down towards the dashed line.
Keep waiting. Do not force the next layer. If it does not cool within 10 minutes, ask the engineer.

alarms.literature: Interpass temperature control and heat accumulation in DED-Arc: Georgousis et al. 2026.
resolution_script: This wait is normal. Do not force the next layer.
Watch the temperature curve go down to the dashed 200 °C line.
Keep the cell door closed so the part cools evenly.
Still above 200 °C after 10 minutes? Tell the engineer.
When the next layer starts by itself, press 'Problem solved'.

alarms.title: Layers getting lower than planned
alarms.operator_message: Each layer is a bit lower than planned. The repair will end too low.
alarms.technical_detail: Layer scan: layer heights 2.0, 1.8, 1.6, 1.4 mm against a planned 2.0 mm. Heat build-up makes the bead flatter. At this rate the repair ends 2.5 mm short of the CAD surface plus machining allowance.

ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Repair below final size after machining.

expected_response.resolved_when: Plan updated with an extra layer, or longer interpass wait accepted.

hints: Hot layers spread out and get lower. This adds up over layers.
Look at the layer height chart: the bars get shorter each layer.
Accept the proposal to add one layer, and let the part cool longer between layers.

alarms.literature: Layer drift from heat accumulation, single-bead models not representative: Georgousis et al. 2026.
resolution_script: The layers get lower because the part is hot.
Open the layer height chart: each bar is shorter.
Press 'Problem solved' and write what you changed.

alarms.title: Dark, rough bead: gas protection lost
alarms.operator_message: Layer 2 looks dark and rough at the edge. Air is reaching the weld. Paused after this layer.
alarms.technical_detail: Gas flow is normal, but the cell door was opened and a draft reached the torch at the part edge. Discolouration (oxidation) and increased spatter at the edge; risk of porosity in layer 2.

ground_truth.root_cause: Draft from the open cell door blew the shielding gas away (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Oxidised, porous layers inside the repair.

expected_response.resolved_when: Door closed, nozzle checked, layer 2 marked for inspection.

hints: The gas is flowing, but wind is blowing it away from the weld.
Check the cell door and anything that makes a draft near the torch.
Close the door, check the nozzle, mark layer 2 for inspection, then continue.

alarms.literature: Shielding and porosity: weld defects document; in-situ defect detection in DED-Arc: Georgousis et al. 2026.
resolution_script: Air is reaching the weld. The build pauses after this layer.
Look into the nozzle and remove spatter.
Press 'Problem solved' and write 'door closed, nozzle cleaned'.
